newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht eases late on dollar rally, weak mood.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht eases late on dollar rally, weak mood.

text.p: The Thai baht, weathering persistent weak market sentiment, eased against a surging U.S. dollar late on Thursday, dealers said.
They said the baht fell to 25.985/25.995 in late trade from 25.970/ 25.980 in early morning.
But the market was subdue in the afternoon with the absence of Singapore players celebrating the Lunar New Year holiday.
"Activities were thin in the afternoon in the absence of Singapore players. Most people were unwilling to sell dollar right now," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the baht/dollar mid-rate at 25.90, its lowest level since June 1990 and against 25.89 on Wednesday.
Dealers said baht sentiment remained shaky in line with a battered stock market and weak economic fundamentals.
